content:
I produced the first accepted Lean-Eval solution to the Conway–Schneeberger fifteen theorem problem. The Lean proof is available in my solution repository. It was produced with GPT-5.6 and Fable 5 in a human-in-the-loop process.

Beyond the final fifteen theorem, the development formalizes intermediate theorems that do not appear to be available in Mathlib and could be useful in other formalization projects. For example, it includes the Legendre–Gauss three-square theorem (Wikipedia; Lean source), as well as representation theorems for several ternary quadratic forms. These intermediate theorems are exposed as separate Lean targets in my solution repository.

Because the development is AI-generated and benchmark-oriented, I do not think the code in its present form is suitable for direct submission to Mathlib. However, these intermediate results may be worth extracting and rewriting as reusable mathematical infrastructure.

Could these standalone theorems be submitted individually to Tau Ceti or Lean-Eval? Are there other suitable places for them?

Lean-Eval submission result: https://github.com/leanprover/lean-eval-submissions/issues/911
My solution repository: https://github.com/KitaKen1/lean-eval-conway-schneeberger-fifteen
Yes, if you can write a coherent roadmap that covers the material that you think should become part of a reviewed and reusable library, then yes, I think we can get some of this into Tau Ceti!
#Tau Ceti > Getting started: roadmaps is the canonical place to ask about writing roadmaps, and to ask for review.
